::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Friday [23 March 1855]  
**From:** Otterbourn  
**Manuscript:** MS West Devon Record Office Acc 1092/12
:::

My dear [Anne](people/person_1582.qmd)
I must write a word or two before Church.  I do not think I dared to expect better than this, and I do hope that at least the suffering is not what it was the day before.[^1]  It is the Cross at least, and she has been bearing it so in patience and meekness all her days that one thinks of her as one made meet.  I am glad that [Alethea](people/person_27.qmd) is coming to you.  I think I am relieved that the violent attack did not come at the periodical time, and that it does seem gentler now.  But I don’t know how to write. [Mamma](people/person_1606.qmd) is well, and liked hearing the N Z journals.  The Selwyns left Hursley too early to be seen, so the Miss Palmers went to meet them at Winchester at 9.25.  [Mrs Keble](people/person_795.qmd) was well enough to enjoy her evening with them.  They went to the Moberlys, & the [Bishop](people/person_1295.qmd) took 9 of the little hands together in his, & blessed them – it was all the young ones except [the baby](people/person_1026.qmd) and [Margaret](people/person_83.qmd), who was afraid.  The [Wigram](organizations/other_157.qmd)s pay all the expenses of the Southern Cross till she or such another reach NZ.[^3]  I say all this because you may be able to care to read it, otherwise it will not trouble you.

I have one of those 4 sermons of the Bishop from himself.  Our good old friend [Mrs Heathcote](people/person_658.qmd) died this morning.[^2]  She had had some sleepless nights, and [Mr Wither](people/person_1544.qmd) thought her failing when he saw her yesterday but she was in better spirits & asked him to send her a fast day service, as they had missed having any at the Park.  I do not think Mamma is knocking up.  She & [Julian](people/person_1624.qmd) have been looking over the boxes of papers almost all day.

Goodbye my dear Anne.  I can only pray for you all.
your most affectionate
CMY

---

[^1]: Anne was nursing her sister [Jane Duke Yonge](people/person_1616.qmd) (1820/1-27 March 1855).
[^2]: Elizabeth (Bigg) Heathcote (1773-23 March 1855), Sir William’s mother.
[^3]: Messrs. Wigram were the shipbuilders who had built the missionary ship, the Southern Cross.
